pr_title: Introduce logging integration for Apache WebHDFS
pr_body:
With this PR I introduce `WebHDFSTaskHandler`, which is based on `S3TaskHandler`. In addition, I've updated the `WebHDFSHook` with the necessary methods and made it provider compliant again.

Closes: #28608

@dstandish I'd like your opinion on this MR, since you have implemented the generic functionality for remote logging.

Additionally, I'd like an opinion on the following issue. The way WebHDFS handles URL encoding changes between 3.1.1 (the version we happen to run) and latest bugfix release 3.1.4, due to these two changes:
- https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-14423
- https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/HDFS-14466

I have now replaced all non-safe characters that come in timestamps with dashes, to be able to workaround this for the most common cases. However, it does does not deal with the full scope of the inconsistency between HDFS versions.

issue_context.title: Introduce a logging remote task handler for webhdfs
issue_context.body:
### Description

We've been using WebHDFS as remote logging solution. The solution we use is adjusted from the [S3TaskHandler](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/4e545c6e54712eedb6ca9cbb8333393ae3f6cba2/airflow/providers/amazon/aws/log/s3_task_handler.py). Since the `apache-webhdfs`-provider is already available and the project already depends on `hdfs`, I think this should be fairly forward contribution.

Before I go ahead and create an actual pull-request, is there anything I should keep in mind with regards to this contribution? 


### Use case/motivation

I'm interested into contributing our internal `WebHDFSTaskHandler`, as I feel the community could benefit.

### Related issues

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [X] Yes I am willing to submit a PR!

### Code of Conduct

- [X] I agree to follow this project's [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/apache/airflow/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

review_comments: `max_retry` seems a bit odd as a param here. doesn't appear used.  maybe remove it as a param and if someone wants to, it could be made configurable via the connection obj

if you look at other file-based log handlers (as opposed e.g. to logging services like ES / cloudwatch) we look to see if there are multiple log files at `remote_loc` -- i.e. it is treated as a prefix.  so there might be `.../1.log` and `.../1.log.trigger.123.log` --  this is how we incorporate files from both the triggerer and the task execution.   

to test this locally you'll probably want to make sure that your webserver does not have access to the local files created, so that it is _forced_ to read from HDFS.

so in any case, in this function you need to discover all the files with that prefix, read the content, and return it in `logs` list which should containe one string element per file

```suggestion
    """A task handler / task log reader for WebHDFS"""
```

the bit that was confusing about the original was this:

> During the run, it will show the executor logs.

not quite sure exactly what is meant there
I'm not a huge fan of how we're creating these nested objects inside of an if/else statement. this feels like a bit of code rot. Is there a way to create a generator class for all of these?

I agree with you, the current solution scales very poorly.

Before I try and implement an improvement, I'm not sure what direction we should take on this. I could create a class/function that does the same switch logic and centralizes the common parameters, `base_log_folder`, `REMOTE_BASE_LOG_FOLDER`, `FILENAME_TEMPLATE` and `formatter`. Is that what you mean?

Adding to that, I feel the issue here is more regarding the non-uniformity of the remote loggers, as I described in my other comment. If we are looking for a better uniform solution, I propose we discuss the remote logging architecture in an issue, as it would be a huge scope creep for this MR.
